Specialized Care for Patients with Special Needs The American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry defines special healthcare needs as “any physical, developmental, mental, sensory, behavioral, cognitive, or emotional impairment or limiting condition that requires medical management, healthcare intervention, and use of specialized services or programs.” Whether your child’s condition is congenital, developmental, or the result of disease or trauma, we can create an individualized healthcare plan to ensure their comfort and keep their smile healthy and bright. Additional Pediatric Dental Services: Here at the Buckeye location, our additional specialized services for kids include preventive and treatment procedures. It allows a thorough examination and treatment, such as laser cleaning, removing decay, and other services. Sedation Dentistry Anesthesia is the foremost procedure in kids’ dental treatment to avoid stress. Most of the treatments involve this practice to get over the dental phobia. Digital X-ray Digital X-rays nowadays help the dentist to examine and take a record of the diagnosis. It also reduces radiation exposure to 80% compared to the traditional X-ray diagnosis. Preventive Procedures Preventive dental practices help maintain good oral hygiene at home. Regular brushing and flossing habits in kids help them prevent baby teeth shedding. Moreover, it helps with the unnecessary cavities in the gums. As rightly said, prevention is better than treatment, so parents must ensure good dental hygiene measures for their kids at home. Restoration procedures Restoration dentistry deals with repairing decayed and damaged teeth. Restoring the shape and strength of the teeth is now possible with crown capping. Get exclusive restoration services and secure your kid’s teeth in earlier stages in a single appointment. Preventive Care for Your Kid’s Oral Needs! This encounter can significantly influence your child’s perspective on dental care, setting the tone for a life of proper oral health and care. GET In TOUCH Pediatric Dentistry includes assessing tooth development,  and assessing the health of teeth that are present in the mouth.  Pediatric Dentists are also trained to provide care for children with complex medical histories, behavioral health conditions, and special circumstances.   Our goal is to set the foundation for a lifetime of healthy teeth and healthy habits. Our office  will guide you through preparing for your child’s first pediatric dentist appointment, including what to expect during the visit, how to deal with dental anxiety, and the steps to follow afterwards for optimal home care. What Happens During the Visit Arrival: Checking In and Waiting Room When arriving at the office, you will be greeted by a member of our team who will assist you with checking in your child for their appointment. The waiting room has plenty of options to keep your little one entertained so they don’t feel anxious about their upcoming appointment.  The waiting rooms also have plenty of reading materials for parents to enjoy while they wait. Initial Examination: Checking Teeth, Gums, and Jaw Once you and your child are called, you will have the option to accompany them throughout the entire process. We believe parents know their children best and we welcome your presence for the initial exam.  The Doctor will perform a thorough examination of your child’s teeth, gums, and mouth.. This includes checking each tooth for cavities, damage, and assessing potential bite alignment issues. The dentist will also examine your child’s gum health, which is crucial as healthy gums provide support and protect against bacteria Doctor Review: X-Rays and Structural Assessment X-rays play a critical role in pediatric dentistry, allowing the dentist to see between teeth where cavities often start and beneath the gums to find cavities that are not visible directly. X-rays also allow the Doctor to evaluate the growth and development of permanent teeth including if there is sufficient space for the permanent teeth to erupt in the future.    X-rays are the standard of care in Pediatric Dentistry and Orthodontics for these reasons. Cleaning and Preventive Care: Importance of Regular Checkups The visit includes cleaning your child’s teeth to remove any plaque or tartar buildup with  specialized tools for children to ensure their comfort.  Regular dental check-ups are essential for maintaining good oral hygiene and preventing cavities.  Regular dental check-ups are also essential in identifying cavities before they cause pain or infection. The Doctor may recommend fluoride application for strengthening teeth and preventing cavities. Education and Guidance: Oral Hygiene Tips for Kids In addition to the physical examination and treatment, the pediatric dentist will spend time educating both of you on proper brushing techniques and overall oral hygiene practices. This includes advice on how to brush effectively, the importance of flossing, and tips on maintaining a healthy diet to support dental health. This guidance is tailored to help you foster good dental habits at home from an early age to ensure optimal dental care throughout life.  Play Dealing with Dental Anxiety: Tips for Parents and Caregivers Creating a Positive Pre-Visit Narrative To help your child feel more comfortable about their upcoming dental visit, our Doctors  recommend discussing the visit with your child as early as possible. Introduce the concept of the dentist in a fun and engaging way by focusing on the positive aspects. Explain the visit using simple, positive language and avoid sharing any negative experiences. This approach helps in building trust and reducing fear associated with the unknown. You can also enhance this process by reading childrens’ books about dental visits or playing games that involve dental care, making the idea of visiting the dentist familiar and less intimidating. As a parent, you have the ability to stay with them during the entire visit to provide encouragement and positive affirmations. Techniques to Alleviate Fear: Games and Visualization Incorporating playful and interactive techniques can significantly reduce dental anxiety in children. Before the visit, you can use the Tell-Show-Play-doh technique, where children are shown dental tools using Play-doh. to familiarize themselves with the instruments in a non-threatening way.  Additionally, smartphone dentist games that simulate dental procedures through animated visuals and sounds can provide a first-hand experience of what to expect during the visit to also help ease anxiety. Role of Pediatric Dental Staff in Easing Child’s Fears The pediatric dental staff plays a crucial role in managing your child’s dental anxiety. The team at PVPD is trained to use age-appropriate language and to explain dental procedures in a way that is easy for children to understand.  The pediatric dentists will explain a procedure and demonstrate it on a model before performing it; this helps children to know exactly what to expect. Additionally, the dental office environment is designed to be child-friendly, featuring special chairs and playful artwork tailored for children to create a welcoming and less intimidating atmosphere. After the Visit: Next Steps and Home Care Follow-Up Appointments and Treatments as Needed After your child’s dental visit, the PVPD team may schedule follow-up appointments to monitor progress or address any additional dental needs. It’s crucial to keep these appointments to ensure your child’s dental health remains on track. If further treatments such as fillings, sealants, or orthodontic referrals are required, staying timely with these treatments is essential for preventing more complex dental issues from developing. Implementing Oral Care Routine at Home To maintain your child’s dental health, consistent home care routines are vital. You should brush your child’s teeth twice a day using a fluoride toothpaste and soft-bristled toothbrush. For younger children, you will need to assist or complete the brushing to ensure proper technique and thoroughness. Flossing daily is also crucial once your child has teeth that touch.  Children do not have adequate dexterity to maintain their oral hygiene until they are able to tie their own shoe laces.  Parents should plan to assist with brushing through the first ten years of age. Importance of Regular Dental Visits for Ongoing Health Regular dental checkups are not just for addressing immediate dental issues but are also essential for preventing potential problems before they become serious. These visits allow the dentist to catch early signs of tooth decay, monitor the development of your child’s teeth, and provide preventive treatments like fluoride applications to strengthen tooth enamel. Ensuring your child visits the dentist regularly, typically every six months, is a proactive step towards maintaining a healthy smile and promoting overall dental health. Regular check-ins with the dentist also help your child build a positive relationship with dental care providers, making future visits less daunting Call to book An Appointment FAQS What occurs at the beginning of a dental examination for a new patient? At the start of a dental examination for a new patient, the dentist begins with an initial consultation and reviews the patient’s oral medical history. Following this, a comprehensive dental exam is conducted and necessary x-rays are taken to assess the overall oral health of the patient. Can cavities be filled during the initial dental visit? Yes, during the first dental visit, aside from other procedures like teeth cleaning, cavities may also be filled if necessary. What are the typical procedures during a routine dental visit? During a routine dental visit, after cleaning your child’s teeth, the dentist will perform a quick check-up of your teeth, examine your gums, soft palate, throat, neck, and look for any abnormalities. Additionally, any x-rays taken will be reviewed.
